transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-01-20T16:00:00Z (UTC)
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Mehta (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, NovaRetail), Samir Khan (Lead ML Engineer), Casey Morgan (Product Manager)

Summary:
Quick migration-focused demo showing API parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood, Console walkthrough (routing, model variants, rollouts), and Optimize recommendations for lowering per-token costs. Discussed onboarding steps, security (SOC2/KMS), and plan to run benchmarks with customer prompts.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, Jordan, Samir, Casey, thanks for making time. I'm Alex Rivera, AE on the Redwood side, and Priya is our solutions engineer, she'll run the deep bits.
[00:18] Jordan: Hi Alex, yeah thanks - excited, we've been looking at how to migrate from our current OpenAI + Anthropic mix to a single, predictable endpoint.
[00:27] Priya: Cool, thanks. Quick agenda, I'll show the API parity layer, how calls map, then a Console tour for routing and observability, and finally some Optimize suggestions for lowering per-token costs.
[00:40] Casey: Sounds good. Our main constraints are latency under 200ms p50 for chat completions, and keeping cost within 20% of current spend. Also we need SOC2 and key management.
[00:55] Priya: Noted. We'll show Dedicated and Private options too.

[01:10] -- API parity demo --
[01:12] Priya: So first, the Redwood API is a straightforward REST/SDK. Most OpenAI-style calls map 1:1; e.g., the "createCompletion" or "chat.completions" style calls map to /v1/generate with model param. For Anthropic and Together, we provide compatibility wrappers so your existing client changes are minimal.
[01:35] Samir: When you say wrapper, does that mean we can keep the same SDK and just flip the endpoint? We have middleware that assumes OpenAI shapes.
[01:48] Priya: You can point your SDK to Redwood and set the model name that most closely matches the capability. We publish a parity sheet - e.g., OpenAI gpt-4o -> redwood-gpt4o-equiv, Anthropic Claude-2 -> redwood-claude-equiv. The response shapes are preserved for common fields but function-calling and streaming have small differences, which we document.
[02:10] Alex: We'll share a parity mapping spreadsheet with exact param mappings and example request/response pairs.

[02:30] [02:30] Speaker 1: Is there an auth change? We use org-level keys and per-route quotas.
[02:36] Priya: Auth is API-key based by default, same model. For Dedicated/Private we support SSO tokens and mTLS for internal services and you can rotate keys via KMS integration.

[03:05] Samir: What about streaming? We rely on token-level streaming for UI snappiness.
[03:12] Priya: Streaming is supported, and we have server-sent events and SSE/WS options. There's a note: some small differences in chunking behavior vs OpenAI but we recommend the same client logic.

[03:35] -- Console walkthrough --
[03:37] Priya: Switching to the Console: top-left you see model catalog, we surface verified performance profiles per model and hardware. Here you can pin a model for a route - e.g., search-route -> redwood-embed-2.
[03:55] Jordan: Can we route by latency vs cost? We want routing policy that prefers cheaper models unless p95 > threshold.
[04:02] Priya: Yes, smart routing policies let you pick priorities (latency, cost, region). You can also set fallbacks: if preferred model is overloaded, it will route to a compatible variant.

[04:30] [04:30] Alex: Observability - per-token cost, per-route latency histograms, and token-level traces. We'll show a sample trace.
[04:45] Priya: Here's an example console trace for a chat session - you can see KV cache hits, batching efficiency, and where latency spikes came from. This is helpful to tune batching and cache TTLs.

[05:15] Samir: Talk about caching - our workload has many repeated prefixes.
[05:21] Priya: Automatic prefix/KV caching is enabled and you can set cache policies per route; that often reduces tokens by 30-60% depending on repetition. For private deployments the KV cache can be colocated.

[05:50] -- Security & Compliance --
[05:52] Alex: On security, we support SOC 2 material, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integrations. For Private we can integrate with your VPC and customer-managed KMS.
[06:06] Jordan: Do you support customer-managed keys in Dedicated? We need to ensure we can revoke keys centrally.
[06:13] Priya: Yes, we support bringing your own key and key rotation via KMS. Audit logs are configurable and you can export them to SIEM.

[06:40] [06:40] Speaker 2: Any data residency constraints?
[06:44] Alex: We do region pinning for requests and can deploy private control plane inside region for enterprise.

[07:05] -- Optimize recommendations --
[07:07] Priya: For cost control, Redwood Optimize suggests batching parameters, quantization profiles (8-bit / 4-bit where acceptable), and model mix recommendations. For example on chat-heavy workloads we recommend a smaller context window model for non-critical prompts and bump up to larger models for final responses.
[07:32] Samir: How do you measure quality regressions with quantized models?
[07:36] Priya: We provide eval hooks - you can run prompt sets through different profiles and get quality deltas tied to prompts. Alerts fire when regression exceeds threshold.

[08:00] -- Parity pitfalls and mapping examples --
[08:03] Priya: A couple of things to watch: tokenization differences (makes prompt length differ), function calling semantics, and safety filters. Example: Anthropic has a different role system, so we map role names and recommend a small adapter in the client to normalize.
[08:27] Casey: That sounds fine, we can add a thin shim. Our main worry is worst-case latency when fallback routing happens.
[08:35] Alex: For fallbacks we keep warm replicas and compatible variants to avoid cold-starts; for Dedicated you can reserve capacity to guarantee p95.

[09:00] [09:00] Priya: Demo time - I'll run a live parity example. Here I have a sample app making an OpenAI-style chat call. We change endpoint to Redwood, set model name redwood-gpt4o-equiv, same payload. Watch the response shape, function call payload, streaming chunks.
[09:27] (typing sounds)
[09:34] Priya: Ok response came back. There is a tiny difference in the metadata field name - it's returned as "exec_id" in one case, previously "id" - that's in the parity sheet.
[09:45] Samir: Minor. As long as it's documented.

[10:05] -- Benchmarks and cost numbers discussed --
[10:07] Alex: High level numbers: for a 10M token/month chat workload we see typical savings 10-30% depending on caching and batching. We'll run a precise benchmark against your prompts.
[10:25] Jordan: We need examples: p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens vs OpenAI baseline.
[10:31] Priya: We'll provide a benchmark report with p50/p95 and cost breakdown. We'll include delta vs your current mix of OpenAI and Anthropic.

[11:00] [11:00] Speaker 3: Does Redwood support the Together models natively or do we need to convert?
[11:05] Priya: We host equivalents and also provide conversion tooling for local weights if you want private on-prem. For Together models we have tuned kernels and quantization recommendations.

[12:00] -- Rollouts & traffic shifting --
[12:02] Priya: Console supports canary rollouts, A/B and automatic fallback. You can route a percentage to Redwood variants while keeping the rest to current provider during pilot.
[12:18] Casey: That is critical - we'll start with 10% traffic and validate.

[13:00] [13:00] Alex: Ok let's capture success criteria: 1) matching functional parity for top 50 prompts, 2) p95 latency under 350ms during pilot window, 3) cost within 20% of current.
[13:18] Jordan: Agreed. Also need legal to review DPA and SOC2 artifacts.

[14:00] -- Questions from customer about network setup --
[14:02] Samir: For Private, what's the network topology? Do we send traffic through your control plane?
[14:09] Priya: For Private deployments you run a private control plane in your VPC; inference plane can be colocated or in your data center. Telemetry and admin plane comms are optional over peered links.

[15:00] [15:00] Alex: Quick recap of next steps: we'll send parity sheet, schedule benchmark, and share SOC2/KMS docs.
[15:08] Casey: Thanks. One last question: what support level for pilot?
[15:12] Alex: We'll include SE support for the benchmark, and AE-level check-ins; Dedicated onboarding includes a 2-week ramp with SRE support if needed.

[15:30] -- Closing --
[15:32] Jordan: Great, thanks everyone, we'll send the prompts and legal contact.
[15:36] Samir: Thanks Priya, that demo was helpful.
[15:40] Alex: Thanks all - we'll follow up by end of week with the doc and calendar invite for benchmark.

End of transcript.
